words.example2Translation: Olimlar yoqilg'i ishlab chiqaradigan mikroblarni yaratishi mumkin.
words.example3: Synthetic biology raises difficult ethical questions.
words.example3Translation: Sintetik biologiya qiyin axloqiy savollarni keltirib chiqaradi.

words.definition: The physical limits on how efficiently energy can be converted. (IELTS ≈ physical efficiency limits · energy conversion limits)
words.definitionUz: thermodynamic limits — energiyani qanchalik samarali aylantirish mumkinligiga qo'yilgan fizik chegaralar.
words.example1: No engine can exceed its thermodynamic limits.
words.example1Translation: Hech bir dvigatel o'z termodinamik chegaralaridan oshib keta olmaydi.
words.example2: There is a maximum efficiency that any engine can reach.
words.example2Translation: Har qanday dvigatel erisha oladigan maksimal samaradorlik bor.
words.example3: Solar panels are approaching their thermodynamic limits.
words.example3Translation: Quyosh panellari termodinamik chegaralariga yaqinlashmoqda.

words.definition: Monitoring people using physical features such as faces or fingerprints. (IELTS ≈ facial recognition monitoring · fingerprint tracking)
words.definitionUz: biometric surveillance — odamlarni yuz yoki barmoq izi kabi jismoniy belgilar orqali kuzatish.
words.example1: Biometric surveillance raises serious privacy concerns.
words.example1Translation: Biometrik kuzatuv jiddiy shaxsiy hayot muammolarini keltirib chiqaradi.
words.example2: Recognising people by their faces worries privacy campaigners.
words.example2Translation: Odamlarni yuzidan tanish shaxsiy hayot himoyachilarini xavotirga soladi.
words.example3: Some cities have banned biometric surveillance by police.
words.example3Translation: Ba'zi shaharlar politsiyaning biometrik kuzatuvini taqiqlagan.

words.definition: Building structures at the level of individual atoms and molecules. (IELTS ≈ nanotechnology · atomic-scale engineering)
words.definitionUz: nanoscale engineering — alohida atom va molekulalar darajasida tuzilmalar qurish.
words.example1: Nanoscale engineering allows stronger and lighter materials.
words.example1Translation: Nanomiqyosdagi muhandislik mustahkamroq va yengilroq materiallar yaratish imkonini beradi.
words.example2: Working with atoms helps make materials both strong and light.
words.example2Translation: Atomlar bilan ishlash materiallarni ham mustahkam, ham yengil qilishga yordam beradi.
words.example3: Nanoscale engineering is used to make computer chips.
words.example3Translation: Nanomiqyosdagi muhandislik kompyuter chiplarini yasashda qo'llanadi.

words.definition: Very clever and original. (IELTS ≈ clever · inventive · resourceful · brilliant)
words.definitionUz: ingenious — juda aqlli va o'ziga xos.
words.example1: The ancient engineers found an ingenious way to move water uphill.
words.example1Translation: Qadimgi muhandislar suvni tepaga ko'tarishning zukko usulini topishgan.
words.example2: They invented a very clever method of lifting water.
words.example2Translation: Ular suvni ko'tarishning juda aqlli usulini ixtiro qilishgan.
words.example3: It was an ingenious solution to a difficult problem.
words.example3Translation: Bu qiyin muammoning zukko yechimi edi.

words.definition: Very basic and simple. (IELTS ≈ basic · primitive · elementary · crude)
words.definitionUz: rudimentary — juda oddiy va sodda.
words.example1: Early humans used rudimentary tools made of stone.
words.example1Translation: Ilk odamlar toshdan yasalgan oddiy qurollardan foydalanishgan.
words.example2: The first people had only very simple stone tools.
words.example2Translation: Birinchi odamlarda faqat juda oddiy tosh qurollar bo'lgan.
words.example3: She has only a rudimentary knowledge of French.
words.example3Translation: U fransuz tilini faqat boshlang'ich darajada biladi.

words.definition: To replace something older or less effective. (IELTS ≈ replace · take the place of · supplant · succeed)
words.definitionUz: supersede — eskiroq yoki kamroq samarali narsaning o'rnini bosmoq.
words.example1: Digital cameras superseded film cameras.
words.example1Translation: Raqamli kameralar plyonkali kameralarning o'rnini egalladi.
words.example2: Film cameras were replaced by digital ones.
words.example2Translation: Plyonkali kameralar raqamlilari bilan almashtirildi.
words.example3: The new rules supersede all previous guidelines.
words.example3Translation: Yangi qoidalar barcha avvalgi ko'rsatmalar o'rnini bosadi.

words.definition: To change something completely and fundamentally. (IELTS ≈ transform · overhaul · reshape · radically change)
words.definitionUz: revolutionise — biror narsani butunlay va tubdan o'zgartirmoq.
words.example1: The steam engine revolutionised transport.
words.example1Translation: Bug' mashinasi transportni inqilobiy o'zgartirdi.
words.example2: Travel changed completely after the steam engine was invented.
words.example2Translation: Bug' mashinasi ixtiro qilingandan keyin sayohat butunlay o'zgardi.
words.example3: AI could revolutionise medical diagnosis.
words.example3Translation: Sun'iy intellekt tibbiy tashxisni inqilobiy o'zgartirishi mumkin.

words.definition: An early test showing that an idea can work in practice. (IELTS ≈ a pilot · a trial version · a demonstration of feasibility)
words.definitionUz: a proof of concept — g'oya amalda ishlashi mumkinligini ko'rsatadigan dastlabki sinov.
words.example1: The small solar village is a proof of concept for larger projects.
words.example1Translation: Kichik quyosh qishlog'i kattaroq loyihalar uchun g'oya isbotidir.
words.example2: The village shows the idea can work before it is used widely.
words.example2Translation: Qishloq g'oya keng qo'llanishdan oldin ishlay olishini ko'rsatadi.
words.example3: Investors want to see a proof of concept before funding the idea.
words.example3Translation: Investorlar g'oyani moliyalashdan oldin uning isbotini ko'rishni xohlaydi.

words.definition: Understood by only a small number of people with special knowledge. (IELTS ≈ obscure · specialist · arcane · little-known)
words.definitionUz: esoteric — faqat maxsus bilimga ega kam sonli odamlar tushunadigan.
words.example1: The lecture was too esoteric for most of the audience.
words.example1Translation: Ma'ruza tinglovchilarning ko'pchiligi uchun juda tor doiraga tushunarli edi.
words.example2: Only experts could follow the highly specialised talk.
words.example2Translation: Juda ixtisoslashgan ma'ruzani faqat mutaxassislar tushuna oldi.
words.example3: He has an interest in esoteric areas of mathematics.
words.example3Translation: U matematikaning tor doiraga tushunarli sohalariga qiziqadi.

words.definition: The history of where an object came from and who has owned it. (IELTS ≈ the origin of an object · its ownership history)
words.definitionUz: the provenance of an artefact — buyum qayerdan kelgani va kimlarga tegishli bo'lgani tarixi.
words.example1: Museums must check the provenance of an artefact before buying it.
words.example1Translation: Muzeylar buyumni sotib olishdan oldin uning kelib chiqish tarixini tekshirishi kerak.
words.example2: Museums need to know where an object came from before acquiring it.
words.example2Translation: Muzeylar buyumni olishdan oldin uning qayerdan kelganini bilishi kerak.
words.example3: The provenance of the vase remains unclear.
words.example3Translation: Vazaning kelib chiqish tarixi hamon noaniq.

words.definition: The belief that history moves towards a particular goal or end. (IELTS ≈ seeing history as purposeful · belief in inevitable progress)
words.definitionUz: a teleological view of history — tarix muayyan maqsad yoki yakun sari harakatlanadi degan e'tiqod.
words.example1: Modern historians reject a teleological view of history.
words.example1Translation: Zamonaviy tarixchilar tarixga teleologik qarashni rad etadi.
words.example2: They do not think history inevitably leads to a fixed end.
words.example2Translation: Ular tarix muqarrar ravishda belgilangan yakunga olib boradi deb hisoblamaydi.
words.example3: The book is criticised for its teleological view of history.
words.example3Translation: Kitob tarixga teleologik qarashi uchun tanqid qilinadi.

words.definition: Early communities that were beginning to develop into towns. (IELTS ≈ early towns · pre-urban communities)
words.definitionUz: proto-urban settlements — shaharga aylana boshlagan ilk jamoalar.
words.example1: Archaeologists discovered proto-urban settlements in the valley.
words.example1Translation: Arxeologlar vodiyda ilk shaharsimon manzilgohlarni topishdi.
words.example2: Remains of early communities that were growing into towns were found.
words.example2Translation: Shaharga aylanayotgan ilk jamoalarning qoldiqlari topildi.
words.example3: Proto-urban settlements developed where farming produced surplus food.
words.example3Translation: Ilk shaharsimon manzilgohlar dehqonchilik ortiqcha oziq-ovqat bergan joylarda paydo bo'lgan.

words.definition: The passing of power from one member of a ruling family to another. (IELTS ≈ hereditary rule · royal inheritance · line of succession)
words.definitionUz: dynastic succession — hokimiyatning hukmron oila a'zolaridan biridan boshqasiga o'tishi.
words.example1: Disputes over dynastic succession often led to civil war.
words.example1Translation: Sulolaviy taxt vorisligi bo'yicha nizolar ko'pincha fuqarolar urushiga olib kelgan.
words.example2: Arguments about who should inherit the throne caused wars.
words.example2Translation: Taxtni kim meros qilib olishi kerakligi haqidagi bahslar urushlarga sabab bo'lgan.
words.example3: The empire followed strict rules of dynastic succession.
words.example3Translation: Imperiya sulolaviy taxt vorisligining qat'iy qoidalariga amal qilgan.

words.definition: An empire that dominates other states. (IELTS ≈ a dominant power · a superpower · a controlling empire)
words.definitionUz: a hegemonic empire — boshqa davlatlar ustidan hukmronlik qiladigan imperiya.
words.example1: Rome was a hegemonic empire across the Mediterranean.
words.example1Translation: Rim O'rta yer dengizi bo'ylab gegemon imperiya edi.
words.example2: Rome controlled most of the region around the Mediterranean.
words.example2Translation: Rim O'rta yer dengizi atrofidagi hududning ko'p qismini nazorat qilgan.
words.example3: Smaller states paid tribute to the hegemonic empire.
words.example3Translation: Kichikroq davlatlar gegemon imperiyaga o'lpon to'lagan.

words.definition: The physical objects that a society makes and uses. (IELTS ≈ physical artefacts · objects of daily life)
words.definitionUz: material culture — jamiyat yasaydigan va foydalanadigan jismoniy buyumlar.
words.example1: Pottery is an important part of a society's material culture.
words.example1Translation: Kulolchilik buyumlari jamiyat moddiy madaniyatining muhim qismidir.
words.example2: Clay pots tell us a lot about how ancient people lived.
words.example2Translation: Sopol idishlar qadimgi odamlar qanday yashaganini ko'p aytib beradi.
words.example3: Historians study material culture to understand daily life.
words.example3Translation: Tarixchilar kundalik hayotni tushunish uchun moddiy madaniyatni o'rganadi.

words.definition: Ancient structures made of very large stones. (IELTS ≈ ancient stone structures · standing stones)
words.definitionUz: megalithic monuments — juda katta toshlardan qurilgan qadimiy inshootlar.
words.example1: Stonehenge is one of the best-known megalithic monuments.
words.example1Translation: Stounxenj eng mashhur megalitik yodgorliklardan biri.
words.example2: It is a famous circle of huge ancient stones.
words.example2Translation: Bu ulkan qadimiy toshlardan iborat mashhur doira.
words.example3: Nobody knows exactly how megalithic monuments were built.
words.example3Translation: Megalitik yodgorliklar qanday qurilgani aniq ma'lum emas.

words.definition: A state that pays money or goods to a more powerful state. (IELTS ≈ a vassal state · a dependent kingdom · a subject state)
words.definitionUz: a tributary state — kuchliroq davlatga pul yoki tovar to'laydigan davlat.
words.example1: The kingdom became a tributary state of the empire.
words.example1Translation: Qirollik imperiyaning o'lpon to'lovchi davlatiga aylandi.
words.example2: The smaller kingdom had to pay the empire regularly.
words.example2Translation: Kichik qirollik imperiyaga muntazam to'lov qilishi kerak edi.
words.example3: Each tributary state sent gifts to the emperor every year.
words.example3Translation: Har bir o'lpon to'lovchi davlat har yili imperatorga sovg'alar yuborgan.

words.definition: The cultural heritage that belongs to a nation. (IELTS ≈ national heritage · cultural inheritance)
words.definitionUz: cultural patrimony — xalqqa tegishli madaniy meros.
words.example1: The government considers the manuscripts part of its cultural patrimony.
words.example1Translation: Hukumat qo'lyozmalarni o'z madaniy merosining bir qismi deb hisoblaydi.
words.example2: The state regards the old texts as national treasures.
words.example2Translation: Davlat eski matnlarni milliy boylik deb biladi.
words.example3: Looting destroys a country's cultural patrimony.
words.example3Translation: Talonchilik mamlakatning madaniy merosini yo'q qiladi.

words.definition: Applying modern ideas wrongly to people of the past. (IELTS ≈ judging the past by present standards · historical anachronism)
words.definitionUz: anachronistic projection — zamonaviy g'oyalarni o'tmish odamlariga noto'g'ri qo'llash.
words.example1: Calling medieval kings racist may be an anachronistic projection.
words.example1Translation: O'rta asr qirollarini irqchi deb atash zamonaviy qarashlarni o'tmishga ko'chirish bo'lishi mumkin.
words.example2: It may be wrong to judge them using today's concepts.
words.example2Translation: Ularni bugungi tushunchalar bilan baholash xato bo'lishi mumkin.
words.example3: Historians try to avoid anachronistic projection.
words.example3Translation: Tarixchilar zamonaviy qarashlarni o'tmishga ko'chirishdan qochishga harakat qiladi.

words.definition: The destruction of religious images, or attacking established beliefs. (IELTS ≈ rejection of tradition · image-breaking · radicalism)
words.definitionUz: iconoclasm — diniy tasvirlarni yo'q qilish yoki qabul qilingan e'tiqodlarga hujum qilish.
words.example1: Periods of iconoclasm destroyed many religious paintings.
words.example1Translation: Ikonoborchilik davrlari ko'plab diniy rasmlarni yo'q qildi.
words.example2: Many sacred images were deliberately broken at that time.
words.example2Translation: O'sha davrda ko'plab muqaddas tasvirlar ataylab buzilgan.
words.example3: The artist was known for her iconoclasm.
words.example3Translation: Rassom an'analarga qarshi chiqishi bilan tanilgan.

words.definition: Relating to the study or collection of old objects and books. (IELTS ≈ relating to antiques · historical · scholarly)
words.definitionUz: antiquarian — eski buyumlar va kitoblarni o'rganish yoki yig'ishga oid.
words.example1: The shop sells antiquarian books and maps.
words.example1Translation: Do'konda qadimiy kitoblar va xaritalar sotiladi.
words.example2: You can buy very old books and maps there.
words.example2Translation: U yerda juda eski kitoblar va xaritalarni sotib olish mumkin.
words.example3: His interest in coins was purely antiquarian.
words.example3Translation: Uning tangalarga qiziqishi sof qadimshunoslikka oid edi.

words.definition: A small part that remains of something that once existed. (IELTS ≈ trace · remnant · relic · last sign)
words.definitionUz: vestige — bir vaqtlar mavjud bo'lgan narsaning qolgan kichik qismi.
words.example1: The ruins are the last vestige of the ancient city.
words.example1Translation: Xarobalar qadimiy shaharning so'nggi qoldig'idir.
words.example2: Only these ruins remain of the old city.
words.example2Translation: Eski shahardan faqat shu xarobalar qolgan.
words.example3: Not a vestige of the old system remains.
words.example3Translation: Eski tizimdan hech qanday asorat qolmagan.

words.definition: Existing from the very beginning of time. (IELTS ≈ ancient · original · earliest · primeval)
words.definitionUz: primordial — vaqtning eng boshidan mavjud bo'lgan.
words.example1: Life may have begun in a primordial ocean.
words.example1Translation: Hayot ibtidoiy okeanda boshlangan bo'lishi mumkin.
words.example2: The first living things may have appeared in the earliest seas.
words.example2Translation: Birinchi tirik mavjudotlar eng qadimgi dengizlarda paydo bo'lgan bo'lishi mumkin.
words.example3: Fear of the dark may be a primordial instinct.
words.example3Translation: Qorong'ilikdan qo'rqish azaliy instinkt bo'lishi mumkin.

words.definition: Greatly respected, especially for religious or historical reasons. (IELTS ≈ revered · honoured · respected · esteemed)
words.definitionUz: venerated — ayniqsa diniy yoki tarixiy sabablarga ko'ra juda hurmat qilinadigan.
words.example1: The scholar is venerated as a national hero.
words.example1Translation: Olim milliy qahramon sifatida e'zozlanadi.
words.example2: People deeply respect the scholar as a hero of the nation.
words.example2Translation: Odamlar olimni xalq qahramoni sifatida chuqur hurmat qilishadi.
words.example3: The site is venerated by pilgrims.
words.example3Translation: Bu joy ziyoratchilar tomonidan ulug'lanadi.

words.definition: To remind people of something in the past, or to be similar to it. (IELTS ≈ recall · evoke · echo · go back to)
words.definitionUz: hark back to — o'tmishdagi biror narsani eslatmoq yoki unga o'xshash bo'lmoq.
words.example1: The design harks back to the style of the 1920s.
words.example1Translation: Dizayn 1920-yillar uslubini eslatadi.
words.example2: The look is similar to fashions from a century ago.
words.example2Translation: Ko'rinish yuz yil oldingi modaga o'xshaydi.
words.example3: Older voters often hark back to better times.
words.example3Translation: Keksa saylovchilar ko'pincha yaxshiroq zamonlarni eslashadi.

words.definition: To be forgotten so that nobody knows about it any more. (IELTS ≈ be forgotten · vanish from the record · be unknown today)
words.definitionUz: be lost to history — unutilib, endi hech kim bilmaydigan bo'lib qolmoq.
words.example1: The name of the architect has been lost to history.
words.example1Translation: Me'morning nomi tarixda yo'qolib ketgan.
words.example2: Nobody today knows who designed the building.
words.example2Translation: Bugun binoni kim loyihalaganini hech kim bilmaydi.
words.example3: Many women's achievements were lost to history.
words.example3Translation: Ayollarning ko'plab yutuqlari tarixda yo'qolib ketgan.

words.definition: The process by which people become isolated individuals with weak social ties. (IELTS ≈ social fragmentation · growing isolation · individualisation)
words.definitionUz: the atomisation of society — odamlar zaif ijtimoiy aloqalarga ega yakka shaxslarga aylanishi jarayoni.
words.example1: Some sociologists blame technology for the atomisation of society.
words.example1Translation: Ba'zi sotsiologlar jamiyatning parchalanishida texnologiyani ayblaydi.
words.example2: They think devices make people more isolated from each other.
words.example2Translation: Ular qurilmalar odamlarni bir-biridan ko'proq ajratib qo'yadi deb o'ylashadi.
words.example3: Community groups can help to counter the atomisation of society.
words.example3Translation: Jamoat guruhlari jamiyatning parchalanishiga qarshi turishga yordam beradi.

words.definition: Signs that the very rich are gaining too much political power. (IELTS ≈ rule by the wealthy · moves towards government by the rich)
words.definitionUz: plutocratic tendencies — juda boylar haddan tashqari siyosiy kuch olayotgani belgilari.
words.example1: Critics warn of plutocratic tendencies in modern democracy.
words.example1Translation: Tanqidchilar zamonaviy demokratiyadagi plutokratik moyilliklardan ogohlantiradi.
words.example2: They fear that wealthy donors control politics.
words.example2Translation: Ular boy homiylar siyosatni nazorat qilishidan qo'rqishadi.
words.example3: Campaign finance rules aim to limit plutocratic tendencies.
words.example3Translation: Saylov kampaniyasini moliyalash qoidalari plutokratik moyilliklarni cheklashga qaratilgan.

words.definition: A small area where people from many different countries live together. (IELTS ≈ an international district · a multicultural pocket)
words.definitionUz: a cosmopolitan enclave — ko'plab turli mamlakatlar vakillari birga yashaydigan kichik hudud.
words.example1: The old port became a cosmopolitan enclave of traders.
words.example1Translation: Eski port savdogarlarning kosmopolit anklaviga aylandi.
words.example2: Merchants from many nations lived together in the harbour district.
words.example2Translation: Port mavzesida ko'plab millat savdogarlari birga yashagan.
words.example3: The capital is a cosmopolitan enclave in a mostly rural country.
words.example3Translation: Poytaxt asosan qishloqlardan iborat mamlakatdagi kosmopolit anklav.

words.definition: The insecurity of work that is temporary or poorly protected. (IELTS ≈ job insecurity · unstable employment · insecure work)
words.definitionUz: the precarity of labour — vaqtinchalik yoki yomon himoyalangan ishning ishonchsizligi.
words.example1: The gig economy has increased the precarity of labour.
words.example1Translation: Gig-iqtisodiyot mehnatning beqarorligini oshirdi.
words.example2: Short-term app-based jobs offer workers little security.
words.example2Translation: Ilovalar orqali beriladigan qisqa muddatli ishlar ishchilarga kam kafolat beradi.
words.example3: The precarity of labour makes it hard for young people to buy homes.
words.example3Translation: Mehnatning beqarorligi yoshlarga uy sotib olishni qiyinlashtiradi.

words.definition: A long period of very low birth rates and an ageing, shrinking population. (IELTS ≈ population decline · a birth-rate collapse)
words.definitionUz: a demographic winter — tug'ilish darajasi juda past, aholi qarib va qisqarib boradigan uzoq davr.
words.example1: Several European countries face a demographic winter.
words.example1Translation: Bir qancha Yevropa mamlakatlari demografik qishga duch kelmoqda.
words.example2: Their populations are getting older and smaller.
words.example2Translation: Ularning aholisi qarib, kamayib bormoqda.
words.example3: A demographic winter threatens future economic growth.
words.example3Translation: Demografik qish kelajakdagi iqtisodiy o'sishga tahdid soladi.

words.definition: The arrogant belief of successful people that they fully deserve their success. (IELTS ≈ arrogance of the successful · pride in merit)
words.definitionUz: meritocratic hubris — muvaffaqiyatli odamlarning o'z muvaffaqiyatiga to'liq loyiq ekaniga kibrli ishonchi.
words.example1: The philosopher criticises meritocratic hubris among elites.
words.example1Translation: Faylasuf elita orasidagi meritokratik kibrni tanqid qiladi.
words.example2: Successful people often forget the role luck played in their lives.
words.example2Translation: Muvaffaqiyatli odamlar ko'pincha hayotlarida omad o'ynagan rolni unutishadi.
words.example3: Meritocratic hubris can make the poor feel looked down on.
words.example3Translation: Meritokratik kibr kambag'allarni kamsitilgandek his qildirishi mumkin.

words.definition: Areas where people build homes without legal permission, often lacking services. (IELTS ≈ shanty towns · slums · unplanned housing)
words.definitionUz: informal settlements — odamlar qonuniy ruxsatsiz uy quradigan, ko'pincha xizmatlardan mahrum hududlar.
words.example1: Over a billion people live in informal settlements.
words.example1Translation: Bir milliarddan ortiq odam norasmiy manzilgohlarda yashaydi.
words.example2: Huge numbers live in unplanned areas without proper services.
words.example2Translation: Juda ko'p odam tegishli xizmatlarsiz rejasiz hududlarda yashaydi.
words.example3: The city is improving water supply in informal settlements.
words.example3Translation: Shahar norasmiy manzilgohlarda suv ta'minotini yaxshilamoqda.

words.definition: The division of society into groups of different status and wealth. (IELTS ≈ class division · social hierarchy · class system)
words.definitionUz: social stratification — jamiyatning turli maqom va boylikdagi guruhlarga bo'linishi.
words.example1: Education can either reduce or reinforce social stratification.
words.example1Translation: Ta'lim ijtimoiy tabaqalanishni kamaytirishi yoki kuchaytirishi mumkin.
words.example2: Schooling may help or hinder movement between social classes.
words.example2Translation: Ta'lim ijtimoiy sinflar o'rtasidagi harakatga yordam berishi yoki to'sqinlik qilishi mumkin.
words.example3: Ancient societies had rigid social stratification.
words.example3Translation: Qadimgi jamiyatlarda qat'iy ijtimoiy tabaqalanish bo'lgan.

words.definition: A lack of interest in public life and politics. (IELTS ≈ political indifference · public disengagement · voter apathy)
words.definitionUz: civic apathy — jamoat hayoti va siyosatga qiziqishning yo'qligi.
words.example1: Low turnout is a sign of civic apathy.
words.example1Translation: Saylovda kam ishtirok fuqarolik loqaydligining belgisi.
words.example2: Few people vote because they are not interested in politics.
words.example2Translation: Siyosatga qiziqmagani uchun kam odam ovoz beradi.
words.example3: Teachers hope to fight civic apathy among young people.
words.example3Translation: O'qituvchilar yoshlar orasidagi fuqarolik loqaydligiga qarshi kurashishga umid qiladi.

words.definition: Extremely rapid growth of cities, faster than services can keep up with. (IELTS ≈ explosive city growth · uncontrolled urbanisation)
words.definitionUz: hyper-urbanisation — xizmatlar ulgurmaydigan darajada shaharlarning o'ta tez o'sishi.
words.example1: Hyper-urbanisation has led to severe housing shortages.
words.example1Translation: Giper-urbanizatsiya jiddiy uy-joy tanqisligiga olib keldi.
words.example2: Cities grew so fast that there were not enough homes.
words.example2Translation: Shaharlar shunchalik tez o'sdiki, uylar yetishmay qoldi.
words.example3: Lagos is often cited as an example of hyper-urbanisation.
words.example3Translation: Lagos ko'pincha giper-urbanizatsiya namunasi sifatida keltiriladi.

words.definition: The passing of money and property from older to younger generations. (IELTS ≈ inheritance · passing wealth down · generational inheritance)
words.definitionUz: intergenerational wealth transfer — pul va mulkning katta avloddan yosh avlodga o'tishi.
words.example1: Intergenerational wealth transfer can widen inequality.
words.example1Translation: Avlodlararo boylik o'tkazilishi tengsizlikni kuchaytirishi mumkin.
words.example2: Children of rich parents inherit much more than others.
words.example2Translation: Boy ota-onalarning farzandlari boshqalarga qaraganda ancha ko'p meros oladi.
words.example3: Economists expect a huge intergenerational wealth transfer this decade.
words.example3Translation: Iqtisodchilar bu o'n yillikda ulkan avlodlararo boylik o'tkazilishini kutmoqda.

words.definition: A theory describing how birth and death rates change as countries develop. (IELTS ≈ population development theory · stages of population change)
words.definitionUz: the demographic transition model — mamlakatlar rivojlangani sari tug'ilish va o'lim darajalari qanday o'zgarishini tasvirlovchi nazariya.
words.example1: The demographic transition model explains why rich countries have fewer children.
words.example1Translation: Demografik o'tish modeli nima uchun boy mamlakatlarda bolalar kamroq ekanini tushuntiradi.
words.example2: As nations develop, both birth and death rates tend to fall.
words.example2Translation: Davlatlar rivojlangani sari tug'ilish va o'lim darajalari pasayishga moyil.
words.example3: Not every country fits the demographic transition model.
words.example3Translation: Har bir mamlakat ham demografik o'tish modeliga mos kelmaydi.

words.definition: The zone where a city meets the countryside. (IELTS ≈ the urban-rural edge · outskirts · suburban fringe)
words.definitionUz: the peri-urban fringe — shahar qishloq bilan tutashadigan hudud.
words.example1: Farmland on the peri-urban fringe is being lost to housing.
words.example1Translation: Shahar chekkasidagi ekin yerlari uy-joy qurilishi uchun yo'qolmoqda.
words.example2: Fields on the edge of the city are being built on.
words.example2Translation: Shahar chekkasidagi dalalarga uylar qurilmoqda.
words.example3: Many migrants settle on the peri-urban fringe.
words.example3Translation: Ko'plab muhojirlar shahar chekkasidagi hududlarga joylashadi.

words.definition: A state in which social rules break down and people feel lost and disconnected. (IELTS ≈ normlessness · alienation · social breakdown)
words.definitionUz: anomie — ijtimoiy qoidalar buzilib, odamlar o'zini yo'qotgan va uzilgan his qiladigan holat.
words.example1: Rapid social change can produce a sense of anomie.
words.example1Translation: Tez ijtimoiy o'zgarishlar anomiya hissini keltirib chiqarishi mumkin.
words.example2: When society changes fast, people may feel they have no rules to follow.
words.example2Translation: Jamiyat tez o'zgarganda odamlar amal qiladigan qoida yo'qdek his qilishi mumkin.
words.example3: Durkheim linked anomie to higher suicide rates.
words.example3Translation: Dyurkgeym anomiyani o'z joniga qasd qilishning ko'payishi bilan bog'lagan.

words.definition: A society governed by old people. (IELTS ≈ rule by the elderly · government by old leaders)
words.definitionUz: gerontocracy — keksalar tomonidan boshqariladigan jamiyat.
words.example1: Young voters complain that the country has become a gerontocracy.
words.example1Translation: Yosh saylovchilar mamlakat gerontokratiyaga aylanib qolganidan shikoyat qiladi.
words.example2: They feel that only elderly politicians hold power.
words.example2Translation: Ular hokimiyat faqat keksa siyosatchilar qo'lida deb his qilishadi.
words.example3: The party has been described as a gerontocracy.
words.example3Translation: Partiya gerontokratiya deb ta'riflangan.

words.definition: The process of a group becoming isolated in one poor area. (IELTS ≈ segregation · social isolation of a group · enclosure)
words.definitionUz: ghettoisation — biror guruhning bitta kambag'al hududda ajralib qolishi jarayoni.
words.example1: Poor housing policy led to the ghettoisation of migrants.
words.example1Translation: Yomon uy-joy siyosati muhojirlarning getto holiga tushishiga olib keldi.
words.example2: Newcomers ended up living separately in one deprived area.
words.example2Translation: Yangi kelganlar bitta qashshoq hududda alohida yashab qolishdi.
words.example3: Mixed housing schemes aim to prevent ghettoisation.
words.example3Translation: Aralash uy-joy dasturlari getto holiga tushishning oldini olishga qaratilgan.

words.definition: Without the right to vote, or without power and influence. (IELTS ≈ marginalised · excluded · powerless · voiceless)
words.definitionUz: disenfranchised — ovoz berish huquqi yoki kuch va ta'sirdan mahrum.
words.example1: Many young people feel disenfranchised by the political system.
words.example1Translation: Ko'plab yoshlar o'zini siyosiy tizim tomonidan chetga surilgan his qiladi.
words.example2: Young people believe politicians do not listen to them.
words.example2Translation: Yoshlar siyosatchilar ularni tinglamaydi deb hisoblaydi.
words.example3: Prisoners are disenfranchised in some countries.
words.example3Translation: Ba'zi mamlakatlarda mahbuslar ovoz berish huquqidan mahrum.

words.definition: A lack of basic things such as food, housing or education. (IELTS ≈ poverty · hardship · want · disadvantage)
words.definitionUz: deprivation — oziq-ovqat, uy-joy yoki ta'lim kabi asosiy narsalarning yo'qligi.
words.example1: Children growing up in deprivation often do worse at school.
words.example1Translation: Mahrumlikda o'sgan bolalar ko'pincha maktabda yomonroq o'qiydi.
words.example2: Kids from very poor homes tend to struggle in education.
words.example2Translation: Juda kambag'al oilalarning bolalari odatda o'qishda qiynaladi.
words.example3: Sleep deprivation affects memory.
words.example3Translation: Uyqudan mahrumlik xotiraga ta'sir qiladi.

words.definition: Believing that all people are equal and deserve equal rights. (IELTS ≈ equal · fair · classless · democratic)
words.definitionUz: egalitarian — barcha odamlar teng va teng huquqqa loyiq deb hisoblaydigan.
words.example1: Scandinavian countries are known for egalitarian values.
words.example1Translation: Skandinaviya mamlakatlari tenglikka asoslangan qadriyatlari bilan mashhur.
words.example2: These nations try hard to treat everyone equally.
words.example2Translation: Bu davlatlar hammaga teng munosabatda bo'lishga harakat qiladi.
words.example3: Hunter-gatherer societies were often egalitarian.
words.example3Translation: Ovchi-teruvchi jamiyatlar ko'pincha tenglikka asoslangan bo'lgan.

words.word: be on the fringes of society
words.definition: To be excluded from the main part of society. (IELTS ≈ be marginalised · be excluded · live on the margins)
words.definitionUz: be on the fringes of society — jamiyatning asosiy qismidan chetda qolmoq.
words.example1: Homeless people often find themselves on the fringes of society.
words.example1Translation: Uysizlar ko'pincha jamiyat chekkasida qolib ketadi.
words.example2: People without homes are often excluded from normal life.
words.example2Translation: Uysiz odamlar ko'pincha odatiy hayotdan chetda qoladi.
words.example3: The artist spent years on the fringes of society.
words.example3Translation: Rassom yillar davomida jamiyat chekkasida yashadi.

words.definition: Trying to gain wealth by influencing rules rather than by creating value. (IELTS ≈ profiting from privilege · lobbying for unfair advantage)
words.definitionUz: rent-seeking behaviour — qiymat yaratish emas, qoidalarga ta'sir qilish orqali boylik orttirishga intilish.
words.example1: Economists criticise rent-seeking behaviour by large corporations.
words.example1Translation: Iqtisodchilar yirik korporatsiyalarning renta izlash xatti-harakatini tanqid qiladi.
words.example2: Big firms often lobby for rules that benefit them without helping society.
words.example2Translation: Yirik firmalar ko'pincha jamiyatga foyda keltirmaydigan, faqat o'zlariga qulay qoidalarni talab qiladi.
words.example3: Rent-seeking behaviour wastes resources.
words.example3Translation: Renta izlash xatti-harakati resurslarni isrof qiladi.

words.definition: Economic policies that help one country at the expense of others. (IELTS ≈ protectionist policies · self-serving trade measures)
words.definitionUz: beggar-thy-neighbour policies — bir mamlakatga boshqalar hisobiga foyda keltiradigan iqtisodiy siyosat.
words.example1: Beggar-thy-neighbour policies worsened the Great Depression.
words.example1Translation: Qo'shniga zarar keltiruvchi siyosat Buyuk depressiyani yanada og'irlashtirdi.
words.example2: Countries protected themselves in ways that hurt other nations.
words.example2Translation: Davlatlar o'zini boshqa xalqlarga zarar yetkazadigan usullar bilan himoya qildi.
words.example3: Leaders agreed to avoid beggar-thy-neighbour policies.
words.example3Translation: Rahbarlar qo'shniga zarar keltiruvchi siyosatdan qochishga kelishib olishdi.

words.definition: The risk that people behave less carefully because they are protected from the consequences. (IELTS ≈ reckless behaviour due to protection · lack of incentive to be careful)
words.definitionUz: moral hazard — odamlar oqibatlardan himoyalangani sababli kamroq ehtiyotkor bo'lish xavfi.
words.example1: Bank bail-outs create moral hazard.
words.example1Translation: Banklarni qutqarish axloqiy xavf tug'diradi.
words.example2: If banks know they will be rescued, they may take bigger risks.
words.example2Translation: Agar banklar qutqarilishini bilsa, kattaroq xavfga borishi mumkin.
words.example3: Insurance can lead to moral hazard if people become careless.
words.example3Translation: Sug'urta, agar odamlar beparvo bo'lib qolsa, axloqiy xavfga olib kelishi mumkin.

words.definition: The way shared resources are overused because each person acts in their own interest. (IELTS ≈ overuse of shared resources · collective resource depletion)
words.definitionUz: the tragedy of the commons — har kim o'z manfaati uchun harakat qilgani sababli umumiy resurslarning haddan tashqari ishlatilishi.
words.example1: Overfishing is a classic example of the tragedy of the commons.
words.example1Translation: Baliqni haddan tashqari ovlash umumiy mulk fojiasining klassik namunasidir.
words.example2: Each fisherman catches as much as he can, so the fish run out.
words.example2Translation: Har bir baliqchi imkon qadar ko'p tutadi va baliqlar tugaydi.
words.example3: Clean air can suffer from the tragedy of the commons.
words.example3Translation: Toza havo ham umumiy mulk fojiasidan zarar ko'rishi mumkin.

words.definition: The process by which new industries replace old ones. (IELTS ≈ innovation replacing old industries · economic renewal)
words.definitionUz: creative destruction — yangi tarmoqlarning eskilari o'rnini egallash jarayoni.
words.example1: Streaming services are an example of creative destruction.
words.example1Translation: Striming xizmatlari ijodiy vayronagarchilikning namunasidir.
words.example2: New online services have replaced video rental shops.
words.example2Translation: Yangi onlayn xizmatlar video ijara do'konlarining o'rnini egalladi.
words.example3: Creative destruction causes job losses but also new opportunities.
words.example3Translation: Ijodiy vayronagarchilik ish o'rinlarini yo'qotsa ham, yangi imkoniyatlar yaratadi.

words.definition: A policy in which a central bank creates money to buy financial assets and support the economy. (IELTS ≈ money printing · central bank asset buying)
words.definitionUz: quantitative easing — markaziy bank iqtisodiyotni qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun pul yaratib, moliyaviy aktivlarni sotib olish siyosati.
words.example1: The central bank used quantitative easing after the crisis.
words.example1Translation: Markaziy bank inqirozdan keyin miqdoriy yumshatishdan foydalandi.
words.example2: The bank created new money to help the economy recover.
words.example2Translation: Bank iqtisodiyot tiklanishiga yordam berish uchun yangi pul yaratdi.
words.example3: Critics say quantitative easing increased inequality.
words.example3Translation: Tanqidchilar miqdoriy yumshatish tengsizlikni oshirdi deyishadi.

words.definition: Problems in production or delivery that limit the supply of goods. (IELTS ≈ production constraints · supply problems · shortages)
words.definitionUz: supply-side bottlenecks — tovarlar taklifini cheklaydigan ishlab chiqarish yoki yetkazib berishdagi muammolar.
words.example1: Supply-side bottlenecks pushed up the price of computer chips.
words.example1Translation: Taklif tomonidagi to'siqlar kompyuter chiplari narxini oshirib yubordi.
words.example2: Factories could not produce enough chips, so prices rose.
words.example2Translation: Zavodlar yetarlicha chip ishlab chiqara olmadi va narxlar oshdi.
words.example3: The government is trying to ease supply-side bottlenecks.
words.example3Translation: Hukumat taklif tomonidagi to'siqlarni yumshatishga harakat qilmoqda.

words.definition: An industry that needs a lot of money for equipment and buildings. (IELTS ≈ an industry needing heavy investment · an expensive sector)
words.definitionUz: a capital-intensive industry — uskunalar va binolar uchun ko'p pul talab qiladigan soha.
words.example1: Steel making is a capital-intensive industry.
words.example1Translation: Po'lat ishlab chiqarish ko'p kapital talab qiladigan soha.
words.example2: Making steel requires very expensive machinery.
words.example2Translation: Po'lat ishlab chiqarish juda qimmat uskunalarni talab qiladi.
words.example3: Small firms struggle to enter a capital-intensive industry.
words.example3Translation: Kichik firmalarga kapital talab qiladigan sohaga kirish qiyin.

words.definition: An economy in which business success depends on close links with officials. (IELTS ≈ corrupt capitalism · favouritism in business)
words.definitionUz: crony capitalism — biznes muvaffaqiyati mansabdorlar bilan yaqin aloqaga bog'liq iqtisodiyot.
words.example1: Crony capitalism discourages honest competition.
words.example1Translation: Tanish-bilishchilik kapitalizmi halol raqobatga to'sqinlik qiladi.
words.example2: When contracts go to friends of politicians, fair firms cannot compete.
words.example2Translation: Shartnomalar siyosatchilarning do'stlariga berilganda, halol firmalar raqobatlasha olmaydi.
words.example3: The report warns of crony capitalism in the energy sector.
words.example3Translation: Hisobot energetika sohasidagi tanish-bilishchilik kapitalizmidan ogohlantiradi.

words.definition: A cycle in which falling prices lead to lower wages and spending, causing prices to fall further. (IELTS ≈ a downward price cycle · a self-reinforcing fall in prices)
words.definitionUz: a deflationary spiral — narxlarning tushishi ish haqi va xarajatlarning kamayishiga, bu esa narxlarning yanada tushishiga olib keladigan aylanma.
words.example1: Japan struggled with a deflationary spiral for years.
words.example1Translation: Yaponiya yillar davomida deflyatsion spiral bilan kurashdi.
words.example2: Prices and wages in Japan kept falling for a long time.
words.example2Translation: Yaponiyada narxlar va maoshlar uzoq vaqt tushib bordi.
words.example3: Central banks fear a deflationary spiral more than mild inflation.
words.example3Translation: Markaziy banklar yengil inflyatsiyadan ko'ra deflyatsion spiraldan ko'proq qo'rqadi.

words.definition: Demand that changes very little when prices change. (IELTS ≈ price-insensitive demand · steady demand)
words.definitionUz: inelastic demand — narx o'zgarganda deyarli o'zgarmaydigan talab.
words.example1: Petrol has inelastic demand because people need it anyway.
words.example1Translation: Benzinga talab noelastik, chunki odamlarga u baribir kerak.
words.example2: People keep buying fuel even when it becomes more expensive.
words.example2Translation: Yoqilg'i qimmatlashsa ham odamlar uni sotib olishda davom etadi.
words.example3: Medicines often have inelastic demand.
words.example3Translation: Dorilarga talab ko'pincha noelastik bo'ladi.

words.definition: The idea that each extra unit of input produces a smaller increase in output. (IELTS ≈ decreasing benefits · smaller gains from extra effort)
words.definitionUz: diminishing marginal returns — har bir qo'shimcha sarf mahsulotni tobora kamroq oshirishi g'oyasi.
words.example1: Adding more fertiliser eventually brings diminishing marginal returns.
words.example1Translation: Ko'proq o'g'it qo'shish oxir-oqibat kamayib boruvchi qo'shimcha daromad keltiradi.
words.example2: After a point, extra fertiliser increases the harvest less and less.
words.example2Translation: Ma'lum nuqtadan keyin qo'shimcha o'g'it hosilni tobora kamroq oshiradi.
words.example3: Studying for too long leads to diminishing marginal returns.
words.example3Translation: Juda uzoq o'qish kamayib boruvchi natijaga olib keladi.

words.definition: A state-owned fund that invests a country's money. (IELTS ≈ a state investment fund · a national wealth fund)
words.definitionUz: a sovereign wealth fund — mamlakat pulini sarmoya qiladigan davlatga tegishli fond.
words.example1: Norway's sovereign wealth fund invests oil money worldwide.
words.example1Translation: Norvegiyaning suveren boylik fondi neft pullarini butun dunyoga sarmoya qiladi.
words.example2: Norway saves its oil income by investing it abroad.
words.example2Translation: Norvegiya neft daromadini chet elga sarmoya qilib saqlaydi.
words.example3: The sovereign wealth fund protects the economy for future generations.
words.example3Translation: Suveren boylik fondi iqtisodiyotni kelajak avlodlar uchun himoya qiladi.

words.definition: A situation of high inflation combined with high unemployment and slow growth. (IELTS ≈ inflation with stagnation · rising prices and recession)
words.definitionUz: stagflation — yuqori inflyatsiya yuqori ishsizlik va sekin o'sish bilan qo'shilgan holat.
words.example1: The oil crisis of the 1970s led to stagflation.
words.example1Translation: 1970-yillardagi neft inqirozi stagflyatsiyaga olib keldi.
words.example2: Prices rose sharply while the economy stopped growing.
words.example2Translation: Iqtisodiyot o'sishdan to'xtagan paytda narxlar keskin oshdi.
words.example3: Stagflation is very difficult for governments to fix.
words.example3Translation: Stagflyatsiyani hukumatlar tuzatishi juda qiyin.

words.definition: Buying something in one market and selling it in another at a higher price. (IELTS ≈ profiting from price differences · trading on price gaps)
words.definitionUz: arbitrage — biror narsani bir bozorda sotib olib, boshqasida qimmatroq sotish.
words.example1: Traders profit from arbitrage between different exchanges.
words.example1Translation: Treyderlar turli birjalar o'rtasidagi arbitrajdan foyda ko'radi.
words.example2: They buy cheaply in one place and sell at a higher price elsewhere.
words.example2Translation: Ular bir joyda arzon sotib olib, boshqa joyda qimmatroq sotishadi.
words.example3: Technology has made arbitrage much faster.
words.example3Translation: Texnologiya arbitrajni ancha tezlashtirdi.

words.definition: The ability to pay all your debts. (IELTS ≈ financial soundness · ability to pay debts · creditworthiness)
words.definitionUz: solvency — barcha qarzlarini to'lay olish qobiliyati.
words.example1: Regulators are worried about the solvency of several banks.
words.example1Translation: Nazoratchilar bir nechta bankning to'lov qobiliyatidan xavotirda.
words.example2: Officials fear some banks cannot pay what they owe.
words.example2Translation: Rasmiylar ba'zi banklar qarzlarini to'lay olmasligidan qo'rqishadi.
words.example3: The company's solvency was in doubt.
words.example3Translation: Kompaniyaning to'lov qobiliyati shubha ostida edi.

words.definition: Relating to government money, taxes and spending. (IELTS ≈ financial · budgetary · tax-related · economic)
words.definitionUz: fiscal — davlat pullari, soliqlar va xarajatlarga oid.
words.example1: The government announced new fiscal measures to cut the deficit.
words.example1Translation: Hukumat taqchillikni kamaytirish uchun yangi fiskal choralar e'lon qildi.
words.example2: The state introduced tax and spending changes to reduce debt.
words.example2Translation: Davlat qarzni kamaytirish uchun soliq va xarajat o'zgarishlarini joriy etdi.
words.example3: The fiscal year begins in April.
words.example3Translation: Moliya yili aprelda boshlanadi.

words.definition: Based on guesses, or involving financial risk for possible profit. (IELTS ≈ risky · uncertain · hypothetical · conjectural)
words.definitionUz: speculative — taxminlarga asoslangan yoki ehtimoliy foyda uchun moliyaviy xavfni o'z ichiga olgan.
words.example1: Speculative investment drove up property prices.
words.example1Translation: Spekulyativ sarmoya ko'chmas mulk narxlarini oshirib yubordi.
words.example2: Buyers hoping to sell later at a profit made houses more expensive.
words.example2Translation: Keyinroq foyda bilan sotishni kutgan xaridorlar uylarni qimmatlashtirdi.
words.example3: Most claims about the future of AI are speculative.
words.example3Translation: Sun'iy intellekt kelajagi haqidagi da'volarning ko'pi taxminiy.

words.definition: Too much of something, more than is needed. (IELTS ≈ an oversupply of · a surplus of · an excess of)
words.definitionUz: a glut of — keragidan ortiq ko'p narsa.
words.example1: A glut of oil caused prices to collapse.
words.example1Translation: Neftning haddan tashqari ko'pligi narxlarning keskin tushishiga sabab bo'ldi.
words.example2: There was so much oil that it became very cheap.
words.example2Translation: Neft shunchalik ko'p ediki, u juda arzonlashdi.
words.example3: The city faces a glut of office space.
words.example3Translation: Shaharda ofis maydonlari haddan tashqari ko'p.

words.definition: Spending money in a careless and wasteful way. (IELTS ≈ wasteful spending · extravagance · overspending)
words.definitionUz: profligate spending — pulni beparvo va isrofgarchilik bilan sarflash.
words.example1: The government was accused of profligate spending.
words.example1Translation: Hukumat isrofgarchilik bilan pul sarflashda ayblandi.
words.example2: Critics said officials wasted public money.
words.example2Translation: Tanqidchilar rasmiylar davlat pulini isrof qilgan deyishdi.
words.example3: Years of profligate spending left the city in debt.
words.example3Translation: Yillar davomidagi isrofgarchilik shaharni qarzga botirdi.

words.definition: The tendency to focus on things that are most noticeable or dramatic. (IELTS ≈ focusing on the obvious · attention to the striking)
words.definitionUz: salience bias — eng ko'zga tashlanadigan yoki dramatik narsalarga e'tibor qaratishga moyillik.
words.example1: Because of salience bias, people fear plane crashes more than car accidents.
words.example1Translation: Ko'zga tashlanuvchanlik xatosi tufayli odamlar avtohalokatdan ko'ra samolyot halokatidan ko'proq qo'rqadi.
words.example2: Dramatic air disasters seem more dangerous than everyday road accidents.
words.example2Translation: Dramatik havo halokatlari kundalik yo'l hodisalaridan xavfliroq tuyuladi.
words.example3: Salience bias can distort investment decisions.
words.example3Translation: Ko'zga tashlanuvchanlik xatosi sarmoya qarorlarini buzishi mumkin.

words.definition: Continuing something because you have already invested in it, even when stopping would be better. (IELTS ≈ throwing good money after bad · refusing to cut losses)
words.definitionUz: the sunk cost fallacy — to'xtatish yaxshiroq bo'lsa ham, unga allaqachon sarmoya qilgani uchun biror narsani davom ettirish.
words.example1: Finishing a boring film because you paid for it is the sunk cost fallacy.
words.example1Translation: Pul to'lagani uchun zerikarli filmni oxirigacha ko'rish yo'qotilgan xarajat xatosidir.
words.example2: People continue with something just because they have already spent money.
words.example2Translation: Odamlar allaqachon pul sarflagani uchungina biror ishni davom ettiradi.
words.example3: Governments often fall victim to the sunk cost fallacy.
words.example3Translation: Hukumatlar ko'pincha yo'qotilgan xarajat xatosiga tushadi.

words.definition: Recognising the limits of your own knowledge. (IELTS ≈ intellectual modesty · awareness of what you don't know)
words.definitionUz: epistemic humility — o'z bilimining chegaralarini tan olish.
words.example1: Good scientists show epistemic humility.
words.example1Translation: Yaxshi olimlar bilishdagi kamtarlik ko'rsatadi.
words.example2: They admit what they do not yet know.
words.example2Translation: Ular hali nimani bilmasliklarini tan olishadi.
words.example3: Epistemic humility makes people more open to new ideas.
words.example3Translation: Bilishdagi kamtarlik odamlarni yangi g'oyalarga ochiqroq qiladi.

words.definition: Predicting how you will feel in the future. (IELTS ≈ predicting future emotions · emotional prediction)
words.definitionUz: affective forecasting — kelajakda o'zingizni qanday his qilishingizni bashorat qilish.
words.example1: People are bad at affective forecasting.
words.example1Translation: Odamlar hissiy bashoratda yomon.
words.example2: We usually misjudge how happy or sad future events will make us.
words.example2Translation: Biz odatda kelajakdagi voqealar bizni qanchalik baxtli yoki xafa qilishini noto'g'ri baholaymiz.
words.example3: Affective forecasting errors affect major life decisions.
words.example3Translation: Hissiy bashoratdagi xatolar hayotdagi muhim qarorlarga ta'sir qiladi.

words.definition: Brain cells that respond both when you act and when you watch others act. (IELTS ≈ empathy cells · imitation neurons)
words.definitionUz: mirror neurons — siz harakat qilganda ham, boshqalarning harakatini kuzatganda ham faollashadigan miya hujayralari.
words.example1: Mirror neurons may help us understand others' feelings.
words.example1Translation: Ko'zgu neyronlari boshqalarning his-tuyg'ularini tushunishimizga yordam berishi mumkin.
words.example2: These brain cells may explain why we feel what others feel.
words.example2Translation: Bu miya hujayralari nima uchun boshqalar his qilganini his qilishimizni tushuntirishi mumkin.
words.example3: Scientists still debate the role of mirror neurons.
words.example3Translation: Olimlar ko'zgu neyronlarining roli haqida hamon bahslashadi.

words.definition: Blaming people's character for their behaviour while ignoring their situation. (IELTS ≈ blaming personality over circumstances · correspondence bias)
words.definitionUz: the fundamental attribution error — vaziyatni e'tiborsiz qoldirib, odamlarning xatti-harakatini xarakteriga bog'lash.
words.example1: Assuming a late colleague is lazy is the fundamental attribution error.
words.example1Translation: Kechikkan hamkasbni dangasa deb o'ylash asosiy sabab izlash xatosidir.
words.example2: We may blame the person instead of considering traffic or other causes.
words.example2Translation: Biz tirbandlik yoki boshqa sabablarni hisobga olish o'rniga shaxsni ayblashimiz mumkin.
words.example3: The fundamental attribution error affects how we judge strangers.
words.example3Translation: Asosiy sabab izlash xatosi notanishlarni qanday baholashimizga ta'sir qiladi.

words.definition: Helping others in a way that ends up harming yourself or them. (IELTS ≈ harmful selflessness · self-destructive helping)
words.definitionUz: pathological altruism — o'zingizga yoki ularga zarar keltiradigan tarzda boshqalarga yordam berish.
words.example1: Carers who never rest may suffer from pathological altruism.
words.example1Translation: Hech qachon dam olmaydigan parvarishchilar patologik fidoyilikdan aziyat chekishi mumkin.
words.example2: Helping others too much can damage the helper's own health.
words.example2Translation: Boshqalarga haddan tashqari yordam berish yordamchining o'z sog'lig'iga zarar yetkazishi mumkin.
words.example3: Pathological altruism can enable harmful behaviour in others.
words.example3Translation: Patologik fidoyilik boshqalardagi zararli xatti-harakatlarga yo'l ochishi mumkin.

words.definition: Influencing behaviour with signals people do not consciously notice. (IELTS ≈ unconscious influence · hidden suggestion)
words.definitionUz: subliminal priming — odamlar ongli ravishda sezmaydigan signallar orqali xatti-harakatga ta'sir qilish.
words.example1: Studies of subliminal priming flash words too fast to see.
words.example1Translation: Ongosti tayyorlash tadqiqotlarida so'zlar ko'rib bo'lmaydigan darajada tez ko'rsatiladi.
words.example2: Words appear so briefly that people do not notice them, yet behaviour changes.
words.example2Translation: So'zlar shunchalik qisqa ko'rinadiki, odamlar sezmaydi, lekin xatti-harakat o'zgaradi.
words.example3: Subliminal priming in adverts is banned in many countries.
words.example3Translation: Reklamada ongosti tayyorlash ko'plab mamlakatlarda taqiqlangan.

words.definition: The tendency to return to the same level of happiness after good or bad changes. (IELTS ≈ hedonic adaptation · getting used to good fortune)
words.definitionUz: the hedonic treadmill — yaxshi yoki yomon o'zgarishlardan keyin bir xil baxt darajasiga qaytishga moyillik.
words.example1: Because of the hedonic treadmill, a pay rise soon stops making us happier.
words.example1Translation: Gedonik tegirmon tufayli ish haqining oshishi tez orada bizni baxtliroq qilmay qo'yadi.
words.example2: We quickly get used to more money and feel the same as before.
words.example2Translation: Biz ko'proq pulga tez o'rganamiz va avvalgidek his qilamiz.
words.example3: The hedonic treadmill explains why buying more rarely satisfies us.
words.example3Translation: Gedonik tegirmon nima uchun ko'proq xarid qilish bizni kamdan-kam qoniqtirishini tushuntiradi.

words.definition: The tendency to think you are better than average. (IELTS ≈ overconfidence · the above-average effect)
words.definitionUz: illusory superiority — o'zini o'rtachadan yaxshiroq deb o'ylashga moyillik.
words.example1: Most drivers show illusory superiority about their skills.
words.example1Translation: Ko'pchilik haydovchilar o'z mahorati haqida xayoliy ustunlik ko'rsatadi.
words.example2: Nearly everyone believes they drive better than most people.
words.example2Translation: Deyarli hamma o'zini ko'pchilikdan yaxshiroq haydayman deb hisoblaydi.
words.example3: Illusory superiority can make people ignore advice.
words.example3Translation: Xayoliy ustunlik odamlarni maslahatlarni e'tiborsiz qoldirishga olib kelishi mumkin.

words.definition: Emotional harm suffered by people who hear about or witness others' suffering. (IELTS ≈ secondary trauma · compassion fatigue)
words.definitionUz: vicarious trauma — boshqalarning azob-uqubati haqida eshitgan yoki guvoh bo'lganlar ko'radigan ruhiy zarar.
words.example1: Journalists covering wars can experience vicarious trauma.
words.example1Translation: Urushlarni yorituvchi jurnalistlar ikkilamchi travmani boshdan kechirishi mumkin.
words.example2: Reporting on suffering can deeply affect the reporter.
words.example2Translation: Azob-uqubat haqida xabar berish muxbirga chuqur ta'sir qilishi mumkin.
words.example3: Therapists receive training to prevent vicarious trauma.
words.example3Translation: Psixoterapevtlar ikkilamchi travmaning oldini olish uchun o'qitiladi.

words.definition: Calmness and acceptance in difficult situations. (IELTS ≈ calm acceptance · composure · serenity under pressure)
words.definitionUz: stoic equanimity — qiyin vaziyatlarda xotirjamlik va qabul qilish.
words.example1: She faced her illness with stoic equanimity.
words.example1Translation: U kasalligiga stoik xotirjamlik bilan yuzlandi.
words.example2: She stayed calm and accepted her illness without complaining.
words.example2Translation: U xotirjam qoldi va kasalligini shikoyat qilmay qabul qildi.
words.example3: Stoic equanimity was considered a virtue in ancient Rome.
words.example3Translation: Qadimgi Rimda stoik xotirjamlik fazilat hisoblangan.

words.definition: Separating different parts of your life or feelings so they do not affect each other. (IELTS ≈ mental separation · keeping things apart)
words.definitionUz: compartmentalisation — hayot yoki his-tuyg'ularning turli qismlarini bir-biriga ta'sir qilmasligi uchun ajratish.
words.example1: Surgeons rely on compartmentalisation to stay calm.
words.example1Translation: Jarrohlar xotirjam qolish uchun hissiyotlarni ajratishga tayanadi.
words.example2: They keep their personal feelings separate from their work.
words.example2Translation: Ular shaxsiy his-tuyg'ularini ishdan ajratib turadi.
words.example3: Too much compartmentalisation can be unhealthy.
words.example3Translation: Haddan tashqari ajratish sog'liq uchun zararli bo'lishi mumkin.

words.definition: The belief that only your own mind is certain to exist, or extreme self-centredness. (IELTS ≈ self-absorption · egocentrism · self-centredness)
words.definitionUz: solipsism — faqat o'z ongingiz mavjudligi aniq degan e'tiqod yoki o'ta o'zini markaz deb bilish.
words.example1: Critics accuse social media of encouraging solipsism.
words.example1Translation: Tanqidchilar ijtimoiy tarmoqlarni o'zini markaz deb bilishni rag'batlantirishda ayblashadi.
words.example2: Posting about yourself all day can make people very self-centred.
words.example2Translation: Kun bo'yi o'zingiz haqingizda yozish odamlarni juda o'zini o'ylaydigan qilib qo'yishi mumkin.
words.example3: The novel explores the solipsism of a lonely man.
words.example3Translation: Roman yolg'iz erkakning solipsizmini o'rganadi.

words.definition: The release of strong emotions, which brings relief. (IELTS ≈ emotional release · purging of feelings · relief)
words.definitionUz: catharsis — kuchli his-tuyg'ularni chiqarib yuborish va yengillik.
words.example1: Writing about the experience was a form of catharsis.
words.example1Translation: Bu tajriba haqida yozish ruhiy poklanishning bir shakli edi.
words.example2: Putting her feelings on paper helped her feel better.
words.example2Translation: His-tuyg'ularini qog'ozga tushirish unga yengillik berdi.
words.example3: Tragedy in theatre offers audiences catharsis.
words.example3Translation: Teatrdagi fojia tomoshabinlarga ruhiy poklanish beradi.

words.definition: The examination of your own thoughts and feelings. (IELTS ≈ self-reflection · self-examination · soul-searching)
words.definitionUz: introspection — o'z fikr va his-tuyg'ularini tekshirish.
words.example1: A period of introspection helped him change direction.
words.example1Translation: O'z-o'zini tahlil qilish davri unga yo'nalishini o'zgartirishga yordam berdi.
words.example2: Thinking deeply about himself led him to make changes.
words.example2Translation: O'zi haqida chuqur o'ylash uni o'zgarishlar qilishga undadi.
words.example3: Introspection is not always a reliable guide to our motives.
words.example3Translation: O'z-o'zini tahlil qilish har doim ham sabablarimizni ishonchli ko'rsatmaydi.

words.definition: Aware of something. (IELTS ≈ aware · conscious · mindful · informed)
words.definitionUz: cognisant — biror narsadan xabardor.
words.example1: Planners must be cognisant of the risks of flooding.
words.example1Translation: Rejalashtiruvchilar suv toshqini xavfidan xabardor bo'lishi kerak.
words.example2: Those designing the town need to know about flood dangers.
words.example2Translation: Shaharni loyihalaganlar toshqin xavfi haqida bilishi kerak.
words.example3: We are fully cognisant of the problem.
words.example3Translation: Biz muammodan to'liq xabardormiz.

words.definition: A person's natural character or tendency. (IELTS ≈ temperament · nature · character · inclination)
words.definitionUz: disposition — insonning tabiiy xarakteri yoki moyilligi.
words.example1: She has a cheerful disposition.
words.example1Translation: Uning fe'li quvnoq.
words.example2: She is naturally a happy person.
words.example2Translation: U tabiatan quvnoq inson.
words.example3: Some children have a more anxious disposition than others.
words.example3Translation: Ba'zi bolalar boshqalarga qaraganda xavotirli tabiatga ega.

words.definition: Habits that are so fixed they are very hard to change. (IELTS ≈ deep-rooted habits · entrenched behaviour · fixed routines)
words.definitionUz: ingrained habits — o'zgartirish juda qiyin bo'lgan qotib qolgan odatlar.
words.example1: Ingrained habits are hard to break.
words.example1Translation: Singib ketgan odatlardan voz kechish qiyin.
words.example2: Behaviour repeated for years is difficult to change.
words.example2Translation: Yillar davomida takrorlangan xatti-harakatni o'zgartirish qiyin.
words.example3: Changing ingrained habits requires patience.
words.example3Translation: Singib ketgan odatlarni o'zgartirish sabr talab qiladi.

words.definition: A strong emotional response that is felt rather than thought about. (IELTS ≈ a gut reaction · an instinctive response · a raw emotion)
words.definitionUz: a visceral reaction — o'ylanmasdan, his qilinadigan kuchli hissiy javob.
words.example1: Many people have a visceral reaction to images of cruelty.
words.example1Translation: Ko'p odam shafqatsizlik tasvirlariga beixtiyor reaksiya bildiradi.
words.example2: Pictures of cruelty make people feel strongly before they even think.
words.example2Translation: Shafqatsizlik tasvirlari odamlarni o'ylashidan oldin kuchli his qildiradi.
words.example3: The proposal provoked a visceral reaction from voters.
words.example3Translation: Taklif saylovchilarda beixtiyor kuchli reaksiya uyg'otdi.

words.definition: A natural tendency to behave in a particular way. (IELTS ≈ a tendency to · an inclination towards · a predisposition to)
words.definitionUz: a propensity for — ma'lum tarzda harakat qilishga tabiiy moyillik.
words.example1: Teenagers have a propensity for risk-taking.
words.example1Translation: O'smirlarda tavakkalchilikka moyillik bor.
words.example2: Young people naturally tend to take more risks.
words.example2Translation: Yoshlar tabiatan ko'proq tavakkal qilishga moyil.
words.example3: He has a propensity for exaggeration.
words.example3Translation: Uning mubolag'aga moyilligi bor.

words.definition: A particular way of saying something. (IELTS ≈ a way of putting things · an expression · phrasing)
words.definitionUz: a turn of phrase — biror narsani aytishning o'ziga xos usuli.
words.example1: The writer is famous for her witty turn of phrase.
words.example1Translation: Yozuvchi o'zining zukko ifoda usuli bilan mashhur.
words.example2: She expresses ideas in clever and amusing ways.
words.example2Translation: U g'oyalarni aqlli va kulgili tarzda ifodalaydi.
words.example3: "Lost in the moment" is a lovely turn of phrase.
words.example3Translation: "Lahzaga berilib ketish" ajoyib ifoda.

words.definition: To speak gently to avoid upsetting people (usually used in the negative). (IELTS ≈ speak tactfully · soften one's message · be indirect)
words.definitionUz: mince one's words — odamlarni xafa qilmaslik uchun yumshoq gapirmoq (odatda inkorda ishlatiladi).
words.example1: The report does not mince its words about the failures.
words.example1Translation: Hisobot muvaffaqiyatsizliklar haqida so'zlarini yumshatmaydi.
words.example2: The report speaks very directly about what went wrong.
words.example2Translation: Hisobot nima noto'g'ri ketgani haqida juda to'g'ridan-to'g'ri gapiradi.
words.example3: She never minces her words.
words.example3Translation: U hech qachon so'zlarini yumshatmaydi.

words.definition: To express something in a particular style or way. (IELTS ≈ express as · phrase in terms of · frame as)
words.definitionUz: couch something in terms of — biror narsani ma'lum uslub yoki tarzda ifodalamoq.
words.example1: The cuts were couched in terms of efficiency.
words.example1Translation: Qisqartirishlar samaradorlik shaklida ifodalandi.
words.example2: The reductions were presented as making things more efficient.
words.example2Translation: Qisqartirishlar narsalarni samaraliroq qilish sifatida taqdim etildi.
words.example3: He couched his refusal in polite language.
words.example3Translation: U rad javobini xushmuomala til bilan ifodaladi.

words.definition: A joke that uses a word with two meanings. (IELTS ≈ a pun · wordplay · a double meaning)
words.definitionUz: a play on words — ikki ma'noli so'zdan foydalanadigan hazil.
words.example1: The title of the book is a play on words.
words.example1Translation: Kitobning nomi so'z o'yinidir.
words.example2: The title has two meanings and is meant to be funny.
words.example2Translation: Nomning ikki ma'nosi bor va kulgili bo'lishi mo'ljallangan.
words.example3: A play on words is very hard to translate.
words.example3Translation: So'z o'yinini tarjima qilish juda qiyin.

words.definition: The idea that the language you speak influences how you think. (IELTS ≈ the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis · language shaping thought)
words.definitionUz: linguistic relativity — siz gapiradigan til qanday fikrlashingizga ta'sir qiladi degan g'oya.
words.example1: Studies of colour words support a weak form of linguistic relativity.
words.example1Translation: Rang so'zlari tadqiqotlari lingvistik nisbiylikning kuchsiz shaklini qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.
words.example2: The words we have for colours may slightly affect how we see them.
words.example2Translation: Ranglar uchun bizdagi so'zlar ularni qanday ko'rishimizga biroz ta'sir qilishi mumkin.
words.example3: Linguistic relativity remains a controversial theory.
words.example3Translation: Lingvistik nisbiylik bahsli nazariya bo'lib qolmoqda.

words.definition: A word that expresses disapproval or disrespect. (IELTS ≈ a derogatory word · an insulting term · a negative label)
words.definitionUz: a pejorative term — norozilik yoki hurmatsizlikni ifodalovchi so'z.
words.example1: "Tourist trap" is a pejorative term.
words.example1Translation: "Sayyoh tuzog'i" kamsituvchi atama.
words.example2: The phrase criticises places that exploit visitors.
words.example2Translation: Bu ibora tashrifchilardan foydalanadigan joylarni tanqid qiladi.
words.example3: Some words that were once neutral became pejorative terms.
words.example3Translation: Bir vaqtlar neytral bo'lgan ba'zi so'zlar kamsituvchi atamalarga aylandi.

words.definition: Taking words from one language into another. (IELTS ≈ loanwords · borrowing vocabulary)
words.definitionUz: lexical borrowing — bir tildan boshqa tilga so'z olish.
words.example1: English has many examples of lexical borrowing from French.
words.example1Translation: Ingliz tilida fransuz tilidan leksik o'zlashtirishning ko'plab misollari bor.
words.example2: Lots of English words originally came from French.
words.example2Translation: Ko'plab inglizcha so'zlar asli fransuz tilidan kelgan.
words.example3: Uzbek shows lexical borrowing from Persian and Arabic.
words.example3Translation: O'zbek tilida fors va arab tillaridan leksik o'zlashtirish ko'rinadi.

words.definition: A word with a special meaning in a particular field. (IELTS ≈ technical term · jargon · specialist vocabulary)
words.definitionUz: a term of art — ma'lum sohada maxsus ma'noga ega so'z.
words.example1: "Consideration" is a term of art in contract law.
words.example1Translation: "Consideration" shartnoma huquqida kasbiy atamadir.
words.example2: The word has a specific legal meaning different from everyday use.
words.example2Translation: Bu so'zning kundalik ishlatilishidan farqli maxsus huquqiy ma'nosi bor.
words.example3: Doctors often use terms of art that patients do not understand.
words.example3Translation: Shifokorlar ko'pincha bemorlar tushunmaydigan kasbiy atamalardan foydalanadi.

words.definition: Words such as "however" or "moreover" that organise speech or writing. (IELTS ≈ linking words · connectives · signposting language)
words.definitionUz: discourse markers — "however" yoki "moreover" kabi nutq yoki yozuvni tartiblovchi so'zlar.
words.example1: Discourse markers help readers follow an argument.
words.example1Translation: Nutq belgilovchilari o'quvchilarga dalilni kuzatib borishga yordam beradi.
words.example2: Linking words show how ideas connect.
words.example2Translation: Bog'lovchi so'zlar g'oyalar qanday bog'lanishini ko'rsatadi.
words.example3: Students should use discourse markers in IELTS essays.
words.example3Translation: Talabalar IELTS inshosida nutq belgilovchilaridan foydalanishi kerak.

words.definition: The ability to use language appropriately in social situations. (IELTS ≈ social language skills · knowing what is appropriate to say)
words.definitionUz: pragmatic competence — tildan ijtimoiy vaziyatlarda o'rinli foydalana olish qobiliyati.
words.example1: Pragmatic competence includes knowing how to be polite.
words.example1Translation: Pragmatik kompetentlik xushmuomala bo'lishni bilishni o'z ichiga oladi.
words.example2: It means knowing what to say and how to say it in each situation.
words.example2Translation: Bu har bir vaziyatda nima va qanday aytishni bilishni anglatadi.
words.example3: Learners can have good grammar but weak pragmatic competence.
words.example3Translation: O'rganuvchilarning grammatikasi yaxshi, lekin pragmatik kompetentligi zaif bo'lishi mumkin.

words.definition: The everyday language spoken by ordinary people. (IELTS ≈ everyday speech · colloquial language · the common tongue)
words.definitionUz: the spoken vernacular — oddiy odamlar gapiradigan kundalik til.
words.example1: Medieval poets began writing in the spoken vernacular instead of Latin.
words.example1Translation: O'rta asr shoirlari lotin tili o'rniga jonli so'zlashuv tilida yoza boshlashgan.
words.example2: Writers started using the language people actually spoke.
words.example2Translation: Yozuvchilar odamlar aslida gapiradigan tildan foydalana boshlashdi.
words.example3: Dictionaries now include more of the spoken vernacular.
words.example3Translation: Lug'atlar endi jonli so'zlashuv tilini ko'proq o'z ichiga oladi.

words.definition: A word with strong emotional or political associations. (IELTS ≈ an emotive word · a biased term · a charged word)
words.definitionUz: a loaded term — kuchli hissiy yoki siyosiy ma'no tusiga ega so'z.
words.example1: "Invasion" is a loaded term when talking about migration.
words.example1Translation: Migratsiya haqida gapirganda "bosqin" yashirin ma'noli atamadir.
words.example2: The word creates fear and suggests hostility.
words.example2Translation: Bu so'z qo'rquv uyg'otadi va dushmanlikni anglatadi.
words.example3: Journalists should avoid loaded terms.
words.example3Translation: Jurnalistlar yashirin ma'noli atamalardan qochishi kerak.

words.definition: A name that is wrong or misleading. (IELTS ≈ inaccurate name · wrong label · misleading term)
words.definitionUz: misnomer — noto'g'ri yoki chalg'ituvchi nom.
words.example1: "Koala bear" is a misnomer because koalas are not bears.
words.example1Translation: "Koala ayig'i" noto'g'ri nom, chunki koalalar ayiq emas.
words.example2: Koalas are called bears, but they are actually marsupials.
words.example2Translation: Koalalar ayiq deb ataladi, lekin aslida ular xaltali hayvonlar.
words.example3: "Free" trial is a misnomer if you must pay later.
words.example3Translation: Keyinroq to'lash kerak bo'lsa, "bepul" sinov noto'g'ri nomdir.

words.definition: The fact that a word has several related meanings. (IELTS ≈ multiple meanings · semantic ambiguity)
words.definitionUz: polysemy — so'zning bir necha bog'liq ma'noga ega bo'lishi.
words.example1: Polysemy can make English vocabulary confusing for learners.
words.example1Translation: Ko'p ma'nolilik ingliz lug'atini o'rganuvchilar uchun chalkash qilishi mumkin.
words.example2: Many English words have several different meanings.
words.example2Translation: Ko'plab inglizcha so'zlarning bir necha xil ma'nosi bor.
words.example3: The word "run" is a classic example of polysemy.
words.example3Translation: "Run" so'zi ko'p ma'nolilikning klassik namunasidir.

words.definition: A newly invented word or expression. (IELTS ≈ new word · coinage · new term)
words.definitionUz: neologism — yangi yaratilgan so'z yoki ibora.
words.example1: "Selfie" was once a neologism.
words.example1Translation: "Selfie" bir vaqtlar neologizm edi.
words.example2: The word "selfie" was new not long ago.
words.example2Translation: "Selfie" so'zi yaqinda yangi edi.
words.example3: Technology produces many neologisms each year.
words.example3Translation: Texnologiya har yili ko'plab neologizmlarni yuzaga keltiradi.

words.definition: The ability to speak or write clearly and persuasively. (IELTS ≈ fluency · articulacy · expressiveness · rhetorical skill)
words.definitionUz: eloquence — aniq va ishonarli gapirish yoki yozish qobiliyati.
words.example1: The audience was moved by the speaker's eloquence.
words.example1Translation: Tinglovchilar notiqning so'z ustaligidan ta'sirlandi.
words.example2: The speaker expressed ideas so beautifully that people were moved.
words.example2Translation: Notiq g'oyalarni shunchalik chiroyli ifodaladiki, odamlar ta'sirlandi.
words.example3: Eloquence alone cannot win an argument.
words.example3Translation: Faqat notiqlik bilan bahsda g'olib bo'lib bo'lmaydi.

words.definition: In exactly the same words. (IELTS ≈ word for word · exactly · precisely · literally)
words.definitionUz: verbatim — aynan bir xil so'zlar bilan.
words.example1: The newspaper printed the speech verbatim.
words.example1Translation: Gazeta nutqni so'zma-so'z chop etdi.
words.example2: The speech was published exactly as it was spoken.
words.example2Translation: Nutq aynan aytilganidek nashr etildi.
words.example3: Students should not copy texts verbatim.
words.example3Translation: Talabalar matnlarni so'zma-so'z ko'chirmasligi kerak.

words.definition: Using very few words. (IELTS ≈ brief · concise · terse · succinct)
words.definitionUz: laconic — juda kam so'z ishlatadigan.
words.example1: His laconic reply was simply "No."
words.example1Translation: Uning lo'nda javobi shunchaki "Yo'q" edi.
words.example2: He answered with only one short word.
words.example2Translation: U faqat bitta qisqa so'z bilan javob berdi.
words.example3: The detective was known for his laconic style.
words.example3Translation: Detektiv kam so'zli uslubi bilan tanilgan.

words.definition: A particular way of speaking used by a group. (IELTS ≈ jargon · terminology · idiom · language)
words.definitionUz: parlance — biror guruh ishlatadigan o'ziga xos gapirish uslubi.
words.example1: In medical parlance, a "bleed" means bleeding.
words.example1Translation: Tibbiyot tilida "bleed" qon ketishni anglatadi.
words.example2: Doctors use the word in their own special way.
words.example2Translation: Shifokorlar bu so'zni o'zlarining maxsus ma'nosida ishlatadi.
words.example3: In common parlance, the word has a different meaning.
words.example3Translation: Oddiy so'zlashuvda bu so'zning boshqacha ma'nosi bor.

words.definition: To have no signs of a serious disease for a period of time. (IELTS ≈ be free of symptoms · be in recovery)
words.definitionUz: be in remission — ma'lum vaqt davomida og'ir kasallik belgilari bo'lmaslik.
words.example1: After treatment, her cancer is in remission.
words.example1Translation: Davolanishdan keyin uning saratoni remissiyada.
words.example2: Her doctors can find no signs of cancer at present.
words.example2Translation: Shifokorlar hozircha saraton belgilarini topa olmayapti.
words.example3: Patients in remission still need regular check-ups.
words.example3Translation: Remissiyadagi bemorlar hamon muntazam tekshiruvdan o'tishi kerak.

words.definition: Protection from a disease that happens when enough people are immune. (IELTS ≈ community immunity · population protection)
words.definitionUz: herd immunity — yetarlicha odam immunitetga ega bo'lganda yuzaga keladigan kasallikdan himoya.
words.example1: Vaccinating most children creates herd immunity.
words.example1Translation: Bolalarning ko'pchiligini emlash jamoaviy immunitet hosil qiladi.
words.example2: When most people are vaccinated, even unvaccinated people are protected.
words.example2Translation: Ko'pchilik emlanganda, emlanmaganlar ham himoyalanadi.
words.example3: Herd immunity protects babies who are too young for vaccines.
words.example3Translation: Jamoaviy immunitet emlash uchun juda kichik chaqaloqlarni himoya qiladi.

words.definition: The spread of a disease from animals to humans. (IELTS ≈ animal-to-human spread · spillover infection)
words.definitionUz: zoonotic transmission — kasallikning hayvonlardan odamlarga yuqishi.
words.example1: Many new diseases arise through zoonotic transmission.
words.example1Translation: Ko'plab yangi kasalliklar zoonoz yuqish orqali paydo bo'ladi.
words.example2: Lots of new illnesses pass from animals to people.
words.example2Translation: Ko'plab yangi kasalliklar hayvonlardan odamlarga o'tadi.
words.example3: Live animal markets increase the risk of zoonotic transmission.
words.example3Translation: Tirik hayvon bozorlari zoonoz yuqish xavfini oshiradi.

words.definition: Two or more illnesses that a person has at the same time. (IELTS ≈ co-existing illnesses · multiple health conditions)
words.definitionUz: comorbid conditions — insonda bir vaqtda mavjud bo'lgan ikki yoki undan ortiq kasallik.
words.example1: Patients with comorbid conditions face higher risks.
words.example1Translation: Yondosh kasalliklari bor bemorlar yuqoriroq xavfga duch keladi.
words.example2: People who have several illnesses at once are in more danger.
words.example2Translation: Bir vaqtda bir necha kasalligi bor odamlar ko'proq xavf ostida.
